blocks.content: The coefficients of the elements of $ $ have a form that may be different from the output of a quadratic regression package. Suppose we have two variables with a mean of zero. Under a Lande-Arnold regression, the quadratic contribution to fitness, w, is $$ \left(\frac{\gamma_{11}}{2}z_{1}\right)+\left(\frac{\gamma_{22}}{2}z_{2}\right)+\left(\gamma_{12}\cdot z_{1}\cdot z_{2}\right) $$
However, many regression packages output the quadratic coefficients as $$ (b_{11}\cdot z_{1})+(b_{22}\cdot z_{2})+(b_{12}\cdot z_{1}\cdot z_{2}) $$

In such cases, $ _ ii /2 = b_ ii $, or $ _ ii = 2b_ ii $, while $ _ ij = b_ ij $ for $ i j $. Failure to make this correction results in the reported $ _ ii $ coefficients being only half their true value, thus underestimating the strength of quadratic selection on $ z_i $ (Lande and Arnold 1983; Stinchcombe et al. 2008). Just how widespread this mistake is in the literature remains unclear, but it may be the rule rather than the exception (at least for papers published before 2008).
